--- title: "[Graph.harmonic_centrality()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Calculate harmonic centrality scores for all nodes. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L26147-L26319){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.harmonic_centrality( mode="out", weights=None, normalized=False, cutoff=-1, attr_name=None, return_dict=False, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Harmonic centrality](/assets/graphs/harmonic-centrality.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The shared seven-node graph shaded by harmonic centrality, the sum of 1 over the distance to every other node. Hub C is closest to everyone and scores 4.83, followed by E 4.50, D 4.33 and B 4.08, while the pendant node G is palest." width="100%"} Harmonic centrality is the sum of the reciprocal of shortest path distances from a node to all other reachable nodes. For unreachable nodes, the distance is considered infinite, and the reciprocal is `0`. This makes harmonic centrality more robust than closeness centrality for disconnected graphs. The formula is: `H(v) = Σ 1 / d(v,u)` for all `u ≠ v`, where `d(v,u)` is the shortest path distance from `v` to `u`. When `normalized=True`, the result is divided by `(n - 1)`, giving the mean inverse distance, which is bounded between `0` and `1`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [mode]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["out"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Direction for measuring distances in directed graphs where: (1) `"out"` follows edges in their direction (default), (2) `"in"` follows edges in reverse, and (3) `"all"` or `"total"` ignores edge directions (only for undirected graphs). [weights]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional edge attribute name for weighted distances. Currently not implemented; uses unweighted shortest paths (hop count). [normalized]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, divides by `(n - 1)` to normalize scores to the `[0, 1]` range. If `False` (the default), returns raw sum of inverse distances. [cutoff]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[-1]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Maximum path length to consider. Paths longer than cutoff are ignored. Use `-1` (default) for no limit. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Column name to store harmonic centrality scores in the node DataFrame. If `None` (default), automatically uses 'harmonic_centrality'. Overwrites column if it already exists. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns dictionary instead of self. If `False` (default), stores in NDF and returns self for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, float], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=` is `True`: dictionary mapping node IDs to harmonic centrality scores. If `return_dict=` is `False` (the default): returns self for method chaining. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Calculate harmonic centrality in a simple network: ::: {#b38636c4 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec # Create a star network graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["Center", "A", "B", "C"]) .add_edges([("Center", "A"), ("Center", "B"), ("Center", "C")]) ) scores = graph.harmonic_centrality(return_dict=True) center_id = graph.get_id_from_label("Center") # Center has highest harmonic centrality scores[center_id] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 3.0 ``` ::: ::: Compare with normalized version: ::: {#dc0749af .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "D")]) ) graph.harmonic_centrality(return_dict=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` {3: 2.5, 1: 1.8333333333333333, 4: 1.8333333333333333, 2: 2.5} ``` ::: ::: Normalizing divides by `n - 1`, compressing the same scores into `[0, 1]`: ::: {#1b51eed2 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.harmonic_centrality(normalized=True, return_dict=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` {3: 0.8333333333333333, 1: 0.611111111111111, 4: 0.611111111111111, 2: 0.8333333333333333} ``` ::: ::: Use with cutoff for local neighborhoods: ::: {#d1d27150 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D", "E"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "E")]) ) # Only consider paths of length 2 or less graph.harmonic_centrality(cutoff=2, return_dict=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` {3: 3.0, 1: 1.5, 5: 1.5, 4: 2.5, 2: 2.5} ``` ::: ::: Chain with other operations: ::: {#2f172847 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C")]) .harmonic_centrality(attr_name="harmonic", normalized=True) ) # Access the stored values ndf = graph.get_node_df() # Returns DataFrame with label and harmonic centrality columns ndf[["label", "harmonic"]] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: For directed graphs, use mode to control direction: ::: {#b92a85ae .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C")]) ) graph.harmonic_centrality(mode="out", return_dict=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=6} ``` {1: 1.5, 3: 0.0, 2: 1.0} ``` ::: ::: Following edges backward instead changes which nodes look central: ::: {#d56149ea .cell execution_count=7} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.harmonic_centrality(mode="in", return_dict=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=7} ``` {1: 0.0, 3: 1.5, 2: 1.0} ``` ::: :::
